newsitem.title: USA: Fuel tank in Texas explodes, killing one worker.
newsitem.headline: Fuel tank in Texas explodes, killing one worker.

text.p: A tank exploded on Thursday at the Channelview, Texas, chemical facility of Howell Hydrocarbons & Chemicals Inc., killing one person and injuring two others, officials said.
The explosion at 7:45 a.m occurred while workers were cleaning the inside of a tank that had previously stored industrial fuel oil. It was not immediately known what caused the incident.
"The tank was out of service and it was being cleaned and there was a flash explosion," said Allyn R Skelton, senior vice president of parent company Howell Corporation.
One worker was immediately killed and two others were in a nearby hospital in fair and stable condition from burns.
Skelton said damage was confined to the tank, which was on the perimeter of the complex, and no gases had been released into the environment.
The complex processes chemicals for third parties and makes research and reference fuels that are used to test lubricants for engines, among other things.
Howell Corporation is a diversified independent energy company engaged in oil and gas exploration, production, marketing, transportation and petrochemical processing.
